note: Hook libraries: Indian Instagram creator patterns (priority 1, Clevertize addition) + the two libraries named in Product Spine Section 4. Patterns only - lines are reference, never copied (M21). Refresh by re-reading the source pages and editing this file; bump 'pulled'. Patterns marked usable:false break a Spine rule and are never offered to the engine.

libraries.source: Clevertize curated — hook patterns common in Indian Instagram Reels creator content (Hinglish), 2025–26
libraries.source_note: Curated from widely used Indian creator formats, not scraped. Patterns only — the engine writes fresh lines (M21). Refresh this list as trends change; bump 'pulled'.

patterns.name: POV opener
patterns.structure: Open on a 'POV:' line spoken to camera that drops the viewer straight into the customer's moment.
patterns.reference: POV: आप दिवाली से 2 दिन पहले फ़ोन ढूँढ रहे हो…

patterns.name: Kisi ne bataya kyun nahi
patterns.structure: Mock-outrage that nobody told them this local secret earlier, then reveal the shop.
patterns.reference: ये बात किसी ने मुझे पहले क्यों नहीं बताई?

patterns.name: Ye galti mat karna
patterns.structure: Warn the viewer off a common mistake in this category, then show the right way (this shop).
patterns.reference: [category] लेने से पहले ये गलती मत करना।

patterns.name: Ruko ruko ruko
patterns.structure: A sudden stop — a character halts someone mid-action with a punchy 'रुको!' and a reason.
patterns.reference: रुको रुको रुको! ऑनलाइन ऑर्डर मत करो अभी।

patterns.name: Sach batau?
patterns.structure: A conspiratorial 'सच बताऊँ?' confession that reveals an honest insight about the shop or category.
patterns.reference: सच बताऊँ? मैं भी ऑनलाइन ही लेता था…

patterns.name: Mummy/Papa reaction
patterns.structure: Hook on a parent's reaction or dreaded question — highly relatable Indian family beat.
patterns.reference: मम्मी को पता चला तो…

patterns.name: Bhai ne bola tha
patterns.structure: A friend's (bhai/didi) recommendation that the speaker doubted and then proved right.
patterns.reference: भाई ने बोला था यहाँ से लेना, मैंने नहीं सुना…

patterns.name: Area-wale dosto
patterns.structure: Direct call-out to people of the locality/town, creator style.
patterns.reference: [AREA] वाले दोस्तो, ये तुम्हारे लिए है!

patterns.name: Unpopular opinion
patterns.structure: State a mildly contrarian take about the category in one line, then back it with the shop.
patterns.reference: Unpopular opinion: ऑनलाइन हमेशा सस्ता नहीं होता।
patterns.rule: No claims the owner didn't give (M22); write fully in Devanagari for Hindi/Hinglish.

patterns.name: Story time
patterns.structure: 'स्टोरी टाइम' — the speaker starts telling what just happened, mid-anecdote.
patterns.reference: स्टोरी टाइम: कल दुकान पर एक आंटी आईं…

patterns.name: Expectation vs reality
patterns.structure: Spoken setup of what the customer expected vs what actually happened at this shop — played as two quick beats in the same place.
patterns.reference: सोचा था एक घंटा लगेगा… हुआ दस मिनट में।
patterns.rule: Spoken/acted, not a split-screen with text (M8).

patterns.name: Things nobody tells you
patterns.structure: 'कोई नहीं बताता…' — an insider truth about buying in this category.
patterns.reference: फ़ोन खरीदने के बारे में ये कोई नहीं बताता…

patterns.name: Challenge / bet
patterns.structure: A playful bet or challenge between the two characters that the shop resolves.
patterns.reference: शर्त लगा लो, यहाँ मिल जाएगा।

patterns.name: Wait for it
patterns.structure: Tease a payoff ('रुको, आगे देखो…') that lands in Scene 3–4.
patterns.reference: रुको… आगे देखो क्या हुआ।
patterns.rule: Only if the payoff really lands later in the film (M27).

libraries.source_title: Trending Hook Formats 2026: AI video hooks in India (published 15 Feb 2026)
libraries.source_note: The article lists 10 frameworks and 10 Hinglish example lines (Product Spine says 12 and 15). It also recommends Hinglish code-switching, festival/cricket relevance, city call-outs ('POV: You just found the best Biryani in Hyderabad') and 'Interval'-style filmi drama.

patterns.name: Problem-first reveal
patterns.structure: Name the customer's pain in one spoken line, then a hard stop, then show the business solving it.
patterns.reference: Struggling with [Problem]? Stop.

patterns.name: Twist reveal
patterns.structure: A character states a common belief, then admits it was wrong and shows what is true.
patterns.reference: I thought [Common Belief] was true. I was wrong.

patterns.name: Jugaad hack
patterns.structure: A clever, low-effort local workaround the business makes possible (home delivery, a quick fix, a fixed slot).
patterns.reference: Free way to get [Benefit] in India.
patterns.rule: No 'free' unless the owner's offer says free (M22).

patterns.name: Secret place
patterns.structure: Conspiratorial line: don't tell anyone about this shop/place - it is our neighbourhood's secret.
patterns.reference: Don't tell anyone about this [App/Place].

patterns.name: List promise (spoken)
patterns.structure: Promise a small number of reasons or tips out loud, then show them as actions.
patterns.reference: Sach batao - ye 3 hacks kaam karte hai?
patterns.rule: Spoken only - no numbered on-screen list (M8).

patterns.name: Price-drop flash (spoken)
patterns.structure: Say the usual price, then the owner's offer price, out loud.
patterns.reference: MRP Rs1999? No, Rs499.
patterns.rule: Only when the owner supplied an [OFFER] with the price. Spoken, never on-screen (M8, M22).

patterns.name: Area call-out
patterns.structure: Speak directly to people of the locality / town by name.
patterns.reference: POV: You just found the best Biryani in Hyderabad.
patterns.rule: Never 'best' unless proven (M22) - use the area name, not a superlative.

patterns.name: Shock stat
patterns.structure: Opens with a surprising statistic.
patterns.reference: 99% Indians ye galti karte hai...
patterns.why: Needs a number the owner never supplied (M22).

patterns.name: Aspirational status frame
patterns.structure: Shows money or achievement milestones.
patterns.reference: How I went from Rs0 to Rs10L/month.
patterns.why: Income claims (M22) and off-tone for a local shop (M3).

patterns.name: Duet / reaction cold-open
patterns.structure: Reacts to an existing viral clip.
patterns.reference: Is this actually possible?

patterns.name: Filmi title card
patterns.structure: Cinematic on-screen title text.
patterns.reference: The Truth About [Topic].

libraries.source_note: Category pages read: problem-solution, relatability-humor, sales-persuasion, myth-busting, urgency-fear. Global, English - patterns are localised by the engine.

patterns.name: What finally worked
patterns.structure: A customer or owner says they tried everything, then shows the one thing that worked - this shop.
patterns.reference: Here's what finally worked for me.

patterns.name: Simpler fix
patterns.structure: Promise that the fix is simpler than people think, then show it.
patterns.reference: The fix is simpler than you think.

patterns.name: Don't blame yourself
patterns.structure: Reassure the customer the problem is not their fault, name the real cause, show the business fixing it.
patterns.reference: Don't blame yourself - blame this.

patterns.name: Is it just me?
patterns.structure: A relatable everyday annoyance asked out loud as a question.
patterns.reference: Who else does this or is it just me?

patterns.name: Everyday 'why' question
patterns.structure: A comic 'why does this always happen' about the everyday moment in Section 2.
patterns.reference: Why does my phone battery die faster when I actually need it?

patterns.name: Don't lie, you've done this
patterns.structure: Call out a habit everyone shares, then show the shop as the easy way out.
patterns.reference: Don't lie, you've done this too.

patterns.name: Every time without fail
patterns.structure: A small recurring disaster (something runs out, breaks) that 'always' happens.
patterns.reference: This happens every single time.

patterns.name: Sell the outcome
patterns.structure: Open on the result the customer wants (a ready outfit, a fixed phone), not the service.
patterns.reference: Never sell a mattress. Sell better sleep.

patterns.name: Imagine
patterns.structure: Open with 'imagine...' and a small, concrete scene of relief.
patterns.reference: Every sale starts with one word: 'Imagine.'

patterns.name: Real over perfect
patterns.structure: Show the honest, unpolished side of the business as the reason to trust it.
patterns.reference: Buyers don't trust perfect. They trust real.

patterns.name: But I'm not...
patterns.structure: A customer voices their hesitation ('but I'm not fit enough...'), the owner answers in one calm line.
patterns.reference: But I'm not ready yet...

patterns.name: You don't need X, you need Y
patterns.structure: Reject a common belief about this kind of business and replace it with the real need.
patterns.reference: You don't need fancy tools - you need this skill.

patterns.name: Told your whole life
patterns.structure: Something everyone believes about this category, gently corrected.
patterns.reference: You've been told this your whole life - but it's wrong.

patterns.name: Don't wait until it's too late
patterns.structure: A small cost of waiting (guests at 7 pm, wedding next week), shown as a moment.
patterns.reference: Don't wait until it's too late.
patterns.rule: No fake deadlines - only a real occasion or the owner's offer dates (M22).

patterns.name: Learned the hard way
patterns.structure: Someone admits a past mistake (bad repair, missed fitting) so the viewer doesn't repeat it.
patterns.reference: I learned this the hard way - don't repeat my mistake.

patterns.name: If not now, then when?
patterns.structure: One short question tied to a real upcoming moment.
patterns.reference: If not now, then when?

local_versions.note: Product Spine Section 4 local-business adaptations (illustrative lines only).

patterns.name: No / Stop opener
patterns.line: रुको! आटा लेने से पहले ये देखो।

patterns.name: Myth-buster
patterns.line: सब सोचते हैं जिम सिर्फ़ बॉडी बनाने वालों के लिए है…

patterns.name: Interval twist
patterns.line: मुझे लगा था ऑनलाइन सस्ता है, लेकिन…

patterns.name: Festival FOMO
patterns.line: दिवाली से पहले ये लिस्ट पूरी कर लो।
patterns.use_with: Any type, only when the film is festival-led

patterns.name: Price-jugaad
patterns.line: Built only from an offer the owner gave

annex_c.name: Area shoutout
annex_c.structure: The owner looks into the lens and calls out the locality.

annex_c.name: Counter question
annex_c.structure: A customer asks the question everyone has ("भैया, उधार चलेगा?"); cut to the owner.

annex_c.name: Everyday crisis
annex_c.structure: Something runs out, breaks or goes wrong at home; a quick cut to the business.

annex_c.name: Myth-bust
annex_c.structure: Someone says a common belief about this kind of business; the owner calmly disagrees in one line.

annex_c.name: Same place, two moments
annex_c.structure: The same kitchen, mirror or phone, first with the problem, then sorted.

annex_c.name: Unexpected action
annex_c.structure: A familiar place with one odd action that stops the scroll (the gym trainer helping an old man tie his shoes).
